gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how much a hardwired soundbar costs at the 48V pack once the reducer's loss is counted: a 30 A reducer at its stated ≥90% efficiency can pull up to about 8.3 A from the pack (360 W ÷ 0.9 ÷ 48 V), and a 200 W RMS bar at full volume pulls about 4.7 A (17 A × 12 V ÷ 0.9 ÷ 48 V). Those currents size the fuse on the pack side. The rivals give only the 12V-side fuse and current.
standout_why: I compared golfcartbase.com (cited), cartvoltage.com, nicksgolfcarts.com, extremekartz.com and blog.burtonacoustix.com. mtx.com (cited) returned 403 and was not read. golfcartbase gives no numbers at all. cartvoltage already gives the two figures that decide the set: a reducer with an input ceiling above 58.4V, and 30A as the minimum with lights (17A at full volume for a 200W RMS bar, 'about 5A from a 48V pack'). nicksgolfcarts already gives the parked-drain problem: 0.25 to 2 A idle draw flattens a pack in 2 to 3 weeks, so wire the reducer through a key-switched trigger. The only thing missing from all of them is the pack-side arithmetic that counts reducer efficiency, which gives the input-side fuse size. That is useful but does not decide the set. The finding that would have stood out, the reducer's own no-load current over winter storage, I could not source from a page I opened.
kit_items: Soundbar: BOSS Audio BRT26RGB, 26 in, amplified, IPX5, Bluetooth. ChatGPT already showed it at $239.98, and Amazon still lists it at that price today.

Voltage reducer: a 48V-to-12V, 30A continuous unit rated for 36–60V input, such as the Hornet Energy HN-VRD-12V-30A (36–60V, 30A, up to 95%) or the FridayParts 30A/360W unit (36–60V, ≥90%, IP55). A 60V ceiling clears the 58.4V lithium charge ceiling that cartvoltage gives. 30A covers the roughly 17A full-volume bar plus about 4A of horn and lights with margin, per cartvoltage. I could not confirm an Amazon listing for either unit.

Pack-side inline fuse: about 10A on the reducer's 48V input lead. The reducer's 30A × 12V = 360W, divided by 0.9 efficiency and 48V, is 8.3A at most. This is arithmetic only; the reducer maker publishes no input-fuse value.

12V-side fuse at the value the soundbar maker specifies (cartvoltage: typically 10–20A), plus a key-switched trigger or toggle on the reducer feed so the bar's idle draw stops when the cart is parked (nicksgolfcarts).
